summary: Cotati packs roughly 7,350 people into just 1.9 square miles, making it one of the tiniest incorporated cities in Sonoma County — yet it sits directly along the US 101 corridor between Petaluma and Rohnert Park, which gives it a connectivity that belies its postage-stamp footprint. Sonoma State University lies just across the city boundary in Rohnert Park, lending a mild college-town pulse to the area without overwhelming it; the Old Redwood Highway strip through town holds a handful of restaurants, a few local shops, and the plaza that hosts the long-running Cotati Accordion Festival each summer. The flat valley-floor terrain means open sky and easy cycling, but don't expect dramatic vistas — the western Sonoma hills are visible in the distance, not underfoot. At a median home value of $702,500 against a median household income of about $113K, the price-to-income ratio hovers around 6.2×, steep but notably less punishing than many Bay Area cities an hour south. Rents averaging $1,899 absorb roughly 20% of that median income, a more manageable ratio. Year-round average highs near 68°F and nearly nine hours of daily sunshine create genuinely temperate conditions, though summer fog from the Petaluma Gap can roll through and knock afternoons back to sweater weather. Most employment pulls outward — healthcare and education in Santa Rosa, agriculture and food production across the county — making this functionally a bedroom community with a short 101 commute north or south. Cotati is essentially a small, flat, transit-corridor town borrowing energy from its neighbors while charging modestly less for the privilege.
